messages:
From: FlowPay Ops <ops@flowpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T08:13:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident report and SLA impact (Feb 13 batch window)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per our ops review, on Feb 13 between 02:40–03:25 UTC a large scheduled batch from our payments pipeline caused elevated tail latency for text-generation calls routed to Redwood’s shared pool. We saw 6.8% requests > 1.5s (baseline 0.6%) and a small number of 5xx retries. The attached incident-20270213-summary.csv has per-region breakdown.

Flow impact: we had to throttle automated reconciliation jobs; customer-facing payment reconciliation was delayed ~18–25 minutes for a subset of accounts. This has commercial impact for us: month-end close and SLAs with our merchants matter.

Request: FlowPay is asking for a remediation credit and a one-month dedicated burst to avoid repeat exposure during their next close window. Please advise next steps and what you’ll propose to your execs.

Thanks,
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Platform, FlowPay
ops@flowpay.com

(attachment: incident-20270213-summary.csv)

Hi Sanjay —

Appreciate the detail and the CSV. I'm circling this internally to scope a remediation credit that reflects the measured SLO delta and the commercial impact you describe. Two quick asks from our side:

- Can you confirm total tokens and peak qps for the 02:40–03:25 UTC window? (a rough number is fine)
- Do you want the dedicated burst for the March close window (Mar 28–31) or earlier?

I’m going to propose a staircase credit model that scales with severity (hours of degraded tail latency × monthly commitment tier) so we can be precise and align incentives. Looping Grace (CS lead) to coordinate the calendar and any technical mitigations.

I’ll follow up with a concrete proposal and numbers by EOD tomorrow.

- Dylan

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident report and SLA impact (Feb 13 batch window)

Dylan / Marissa —

I validated the customer tokens and peak qps from our logs: roughly 3.4M tokens and a short burst to 420 qps during the window; most of their traffic is on our shared pool. I also confirmed the FlowPay PROD logs snippet shows repeated retrying clients which amplified queuing.

For a remediation construct that’s fair and repeatable, my recommended structure: a 3-step staircase credit tied to measurable impact:

1) Tier A (minimal): <2% SLA delta — 10% monthly credit pro-rated to affected customers (small operational impact)
2) Tier B (moderate): 2–5% SLA delta — 25% credit + one-time 100k token bill credit
3) Tier C (severe): >5% SLA delta — 50% credit + one-month free dedicated burst (capped to 32 GPUs)

Given FlowPay’s 6.8% tail >1.5s, they land in Tier C nominally. Financially that maps to ~1.8% of their monthly spend as an immediate line-item concession plus the operational cost of the dedicated burst. I attached a worked example (slo-impact-staircase-calcs.xlsx).

We should get exec signoff for Tier C here because it includes a free capacity allocation.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success — Platform
Redwood Inference
(attachment: slo-impact-staircase-calcs.xlsx)

Subject: Fwd: SLA concession: proposed staircase credit scheme for Feb 13 batch incident

Marissa —

Forwarding the thread and Grace's recommended Tier C for FlowPay (they exceed the >5% threshold). Finance flagged two points we need leadership approval for: 1) a one-month free dedicated burst (capped at 32 GPUs) and 2) the accounting treatment — treat the token credit as contra-revenue (one-off) or as a prepaid credit against future usage? Finance prefers contra-revenue.

My recommendation: approve the Tier C concession as a one-off goodwill remediation but record as contra-revenue. FlowPay is strategic (payments vertical) and this preserves our relationship ahead of their Q2 ramp. If approved, I'll draft the concession letter and HubSpot note.

Karthik

Karthik / team —

Approved on a conditional basis. Approve the Tier C remediation: 50% credit on the affected month (applied as contra-revenue) + one-month dedicated burst (32 GPU cap) to be scheduled for Mar 28–31. Conditions:

- We include a short root-cause summary and a commitment from FlowPay to run their large batch jobs in the dedicated window if they want the burst in future months.
- Legal to sign a concession letter with the credit terms and a clause that this is a one-off concession for the Feb 13 event.
- CS to confirm the dedicated pool configuration; ops to ensure isolation during the burst.

Marissa
